name: Lal Masjid (exterior)
assumptions: Hall plan 36 by 24.7 m, turned 16.2 degrees off the enclosure to face the qibla: measured from Esri imagery, about 1 m accuracy; the Open Buildings 858 m2 roof agrees.
Wall height 7 m from the dossier (low confidence); frieze and window heights are fractions read from the 2013 photo.
Dome base radius 5.75 m from the satellite image; apex 14 m fitted to the 2013 and postcard proportions. No published dimension. No finial is visible in any photo.

Minaret tips 26.5 m: about 4 times the wall height on the 1971 postcards, trimmed to the 2013 photo; heights not published. Gallery heights fitted to the postcards and the 2018 photo; the lowest gallery is seen only on the 1971 postcards and is assumed to survive.
Minaret feet placed at the middle of their satellite image strokes, so each may be up to 3 m out; set symmetric about the dome axis.

The 2013 photo is read as the south-west face (the minaret sits behind the dome shoulder only from there) and the 2018 photo as the north-west face: window and panel order come from those, spacing estimated.
South-east hall face was not photographed: it repeats the buff wall, frieze and arched windows.
North-east face, verandah walls, central porch and courtyard wings were not photographed since 1971: buff walls and heights are estimates; the porch arch comes from the 1971 postcards.
Calligraphy panel is drawn as abstract pale blocks and an ochre disc, and the sign carries no lettering: the real text is not reproduced.
Grille on the two street boundaries where photographed; the other two sides are a plain 2.2 m red wall. Sheds and the courtyard shade structures inside the enclosure are left out.
Lighting unknown: window glow is a guess.
